title: Keep test data separate
summary: A test set holds examples kept out of model fitting. It gives a better check than only asking about examples the model already saw.
introduction: A test set holds examples kept out of model fitting. It gives a better check than only asking about examples the model already saw. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A test set holds examples kept out of model fitting. It gives a better check than only asking about examples the model already saw.

blocks.code:
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
X = [[n] for n in range(10)]
y = [0] * 5 + [1] * 5
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=0, stratify=y)
print(len(X_train), len(X_test))
blocks.title: Keep test data separate

blocks.text: The output is 8 2. Two examples are held out. stratify helps preserve the class proportions for this split.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Repeatedly choosing changes based on test results can leak information from the test set.
